entries.subject: Lucy L’LORRI photographs as a photographic lens
entries.finding: PR #182 already includes the recovered TEMPEST numerical shape. PRs #189 and #190 supply the shared photograph pipeline and correct L’LORRI target binding. Six native Dinkinesh frames decode, but full-image, regional and additional-view registration trials remain unqualified; no photographic lens has been baked. The latest independent native-overlap check has 16 holdouts, 2.0284 px RMS and 4.7434 px maximum under the existing 1 px RMS limit.
entries.revisitWhen: New mesh-frame or camera/control-network evidence, a finer compatible source mesh, or a specifically demonstrated defect in the existing projection/matching code. Import support alone is now verified and does not justify repeating unchanged registration trials.

entries.subject: Recovered TEMPEST Dinkinesh STL
entries.finding: The displayed TEMPEST dataset uses the preserved 635-vertex, 1,266-face mesh from public Git history. Its original metre coordinates give a 737.508 m equivalent diameter. This is a selected numerical shape, not a qualified photographic frame.

entries.subject: Celestia authored model and contributed texture
entries.finding: The alternative shape dataset retains the CC BY 4.0 authored reconstruction. Its unqualified contributed texture is excluded; detailed relief and the unseen hemisphere remain approximations. Existing Gazetteer places stay on this dataset.

entries.subject: TEMPEST history, configuration and flyby companions
entries.finding: Historical shape inventory, file history, release assets and configuration did not supply a finer Dinkinesh mesh or a mission-registered camera. The earlier flyby script uses a simplified trajectory and a private configuration absent from the public tree. Configuration spin axes without an epoch do not establish this STL’s mission frame.
entries.revisitWhen: A changed public release, linked numeric mesh, camera table or epoch-bound frame declaration matching the selected STL.

entries.subject: Mission shape papers and accessible supplementary material
entries.finding: The papers describe finer numerical models and registered imagery, but the examined publications and accessible supplements did not supply their mesh connectivity and matched cameras. Jackson’s 5,186-facet derivative is distinct from the recovered 1,266-face STL. A promised archive release is not proof that the files were located.
entries.revisitWhen: A released numeric shape, backplane, control-point or camera bundle associated with one of these papers.

entries.subject: PDS catalogue and Lucy DSK inventories
entries.finding: The recorded catalogue query and both examined DSK directories exposed no Dinkinesh shape product; the DSK listings contained Donaldjohanson. This is a bounded inventory result, not a claim that no Dinkinesh model exists.
entries.revisitWhen: A new Dinkinesh collection, DSK entry, label or linked released mesh.

entries.subject: SBMT Dinkinesh mesh and registered observations
entries.finding: The paper describes co-registered Dinkinesh imagery in SBMT. The examined data endpoint requested authentication, so its mesh/camera contents were not inspected. Access failure does not establish missing data.
entries.revisitWhen: A public release or authorized accessible SBMT dataset with its mesh and image geometry.

entries.subject: Six partially processed Lucy L’LORRI FITS observations
entries.finding: Frames 9545, 9587, 9602, 9617, 9632 and 9722 decode through the shared reader at PR #190, each with 1,046,433 accepted and 2,143 rejected detector pixels. Wrong-target binding is rejected. Values are relative DN per second, not I/F. The retained report proves decoding and target binding only; photographic registration remains unresolved.
entries.revisitWhen: A qualified source-mesh camera solution. Recheck decoding only when the native product, decoder or declared target changes.

entries.subject: Corrected Lucy SPK and TAN-SIP header geometry
entries.finding: The corrected reconstruction SPK agrees with CSPICE through SpiceyPy at three tested observation midpoints. It corrects the trajectory problem documented in the archive timing note, while neither it nor TAN-SIP headers establishes the recovered mesh’s prime meridian or phase.
entries.revisitWhen: A matching body-frame registration or evidence of a specific timing/aberration interpretation error.

entries.subject: dinkinesh_v10.tpc body orientation
entries.finding: The examined kernel explicitly retains a placeholder pole and pre-encounter 52.67-hour period. It is unsuitable for orienting the recovered mesh. The published pole and 3.737-hour period still leave its phase and prime meridian unqualified.
entries.revisitWhen: A revised, non-placeholder orientation kernel demonstrably matching this mesh.

entries.subject: Outline-based orientation and pointing trials
entries.finding: Pinhole and distortion-aware limb trials did not establish internal terrain alignment. A prior apparent pass sampled only part of the outline; fixing that defect changed its holdout RMS from 2.161 to 5.506 px. The historical report preserves the failed multi-view checks and the correction.
entries.revisitWhen: New independent terrain/frame evidence. An outline fit alone cannot reopen the photographic lens.

entries.subject: Frozen central region and native-image controls
entries.finding: The earlier crop altered pixels before convolution and its apparent improvement is superseded. Selecting the same region after full-image convolution leaves 14 independent-view holdouts with 1.1861 px RMS. A rigid regional trial also fails the additional view. The region does not qualify a photographic lens.
entries.revisitWhen: A specific upstream registration fix or compatible finer shape; do not trim failing holdouts or change the frozen region to obtain a pass.

entries.subject: Paired native-feature depths versus the coarse source mesh
entries.finding: The two surrounding views provide 56 shared feature pairs: conditional median absolute mesh-depth difference 6.47 m and median paired-depth disagreement 1.43 m. The correlation supports a coarse-shape limitation hypothesis; inferred cameras prevent an absolute mesh-accuracy claim.
entries.revisitWhen: A finer source mesh, independent camera/control solution or counterevidence that separates camera bias from missing shape detail.

entries.subject: Dinkinesh–Selam formation simulation releases
entries.finding: The examined Dinkinesh-Selam_formation v1.3 and Binary_Diversity v1.1 inventories contain simulation code and numerical simulation/source data, not a located mission-registered Dinkinesh shape. Their boulder or particle coordinates are not accepted as observed terrain.
entries.revisitWhen: A documented observed mesh or mission registration product in a subsequent release.
